source_text.body:
Write unit tests and add AI review to a CI/CD pipeline
Author used Copilot agent mode to write unit tests and wired Copilot review and failure analysis into CI/CD, reporting CI test failures fell from 18% to 9%.
Done with
GH
GitHub Copilot
What they did
On a Node.js microservice, the author assigned GitHub issues to Copilot's coding agent. It opened draft PRs with unit tests, and the author left review comments that it then addressed. In week 3 they edited the GitHub Actions workflow to add Copilot review, test-failure analysis and vulnerability-fix steps. Branch protection kept human review in place.
How it went
Over two weeks, CI test failures fell from 18% to 9% and average time to merge from 4.2 to 2.1 hours. Failures included a payment refactor that broke 47 tests and a dependency update that got stuck.
Worth knowing
The workflow's gh copilot review, fix and analyze-failures commands may not exist as shown, so check them first. The results are the author's own rough figures from two weeks.
Try it yourself
with
GitHub Copilot
Copy prompt
In [owner/repo], write unit tests for [module or folder] to cover the main paths and edge cases, using [test framework]. Then add a CI step that runs Copilot code review on each pull request and summarizes any test failures. You are done when the tests pass locally and in CI, and show me the workflow file changes before you commit them.
Original source: https://dev.to/gaikwadshri29/agentic-devops-i-let-github-copilot-run-my-entire-cicd-pipeline-and-lived-to-tell-the-tale-50oh
